outputs.exact_statement: There exist a finitely generated discrete group $G_{\mathrm{sur}}$ and a projection $b_0\in C_r^*(G_{\mathrm{sur}})$ with irrational canonical trace. Moreover, $$[b_0]\notin\mu_0^{G_{\mathrm{sur}}}\bigl(K_0^{G_{\mathrm{sur}}}(\underline EG_{\mathrm{sur}})\bigr).$$ In particular, the coefficient-free reduced Baum–Connes conjecture for countable discrete groups is false.
For every countable discrete group $G$, $$\tau_{G*}\!\left(\mu_0^G(K_0^G(\underline EG))\right)\subseteq\mathbb Q.$$
Different indexed copies cannot share a simple edge path of length at least $\lambda\sigma(P)$ in either copy $P$. In particular, different index pairs give different labelled subgraphs.

In a diagram chosen as above, the following hold.*

1.  *Every bounded face assigned to $P$ has perimeter at least $\sigma(P)$. Every arc incident to that face has original length less than $\lambda\sigma(P)$.*

2.  *More generally, an arc with different copy assignments on its two incidences has length less than $\lambda\sigma(Q)$ for either assignment $Q$. An arc with a generator-side incidence has length one.*


3.  *The compressed diagram satisfies $$\label{eq:diagram-count}
    (1/\lambda-6)F\le6m-6,\qquad b\le6m.$$

There is an integer $D_0$, independent of all the above data, such that every vertex on a geodesic triangle in $\widehat X$ is within $D_0$ of a vertex on another side. Moreover:* 1. * If an edge path of length $L$ joins $x,a\in P$ while avoiding $c_P$, then $$\label{eq:avoidance} d_P(x,a)\le12(L+1)\lambda\sigma(P).$$* 2. *If $\lambda<1/12$, the graph $X$ is simple: no nonfreely-trivial closed label word in $X$ has length at most two.

Let $R$ be a group vertex or a center of $\widehat X$, and let $A=c_P\ne R$. Choose one geodesic from $A$ to $R$, whose first group vertex is $a\in P$. Every vertex shared by $P$ and any *different* copy $Q$ with $$d_{\widehat X}(c_Q,R)\le d_{\widehat X}(c_P,R)$$ lies in the intrinsic induced ball $B_P$ about $a$ of radius $$\label{eq:overlap-radius}
r_P=\left\lfloor12(L_0+1)\lambda\sigma(P)\right\rfloor.$$

The inclusions of the copies give an internal algebraic direct sum $$\label{eq:cycle-sum}
Z_1(X;\mathbb F_2)=\bigoplus_P Z_1(P;\mathbb F_2).$$

For every $i$ there is a $k_i$-dimensional subspace $C_i\subseteq\mathbb F_p^{\operatorname{Vert}(\Theta_i)}$ such that $w_i\in C_i$ and $$|\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}z|>\eta n_i
  \qquad
  \text{for every nonzero }z\in C_i\cup C_i^\perp.$$

If $P$ is invalid for $\omega$, then every subset $B\subseteq P$ satisfies $$d|B|-2e_{\omega,P}(B)\ge c|B|.
 \label{eq:local-deficit}$$

For every $\omega\in\Omega$ and every finite set $Y\subseteq U_\omega$, let $A$ be the graph on $Y$ consisting of all its internal enabled edges. Then $$d|Y|-2|E(A)|\ge(c/2)|Y|.
 \label{eq:global-deficit}$$

For every $\omega\in\Omega$, the restriction of $\pi_\omega(T)$ to $\ell^2(U_\omega)$ satisfies $$\pi_\omega(T)|_{\ell^2(U_\omega)}\ge\frac{c^2}{8d}I.
 \label{eq:remaining-spectral-bound}$$ Put $$\varepsilon=\min\{\rho,c^2/(8d)\}>0.$$ Then $$\mathop{\mathrm{spec}}(\pi_\omega(T))\subseteq\{0\}\cup[\varepsilon,2d],
 \label{eq:uniform-spectrum}$$ and its kernel is exactly the Hilbert-space direct sum of the one-dimensional spaces of constants on the valid copies.

There exists a projection $b_0\in C_r^*(G_{\mathrm{sur}})$ such that, for every $\omega\in\Omega$, $\pi_\omega(b_0)$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\ker\pi_\omega(T)$. Explicitly, it is projection onto constants on each valid copy and is zero on $\ell^2(U_\omega)$. In particular, $$\langle\pi_\omega(b_0)\delta_1,\delta_1\rangle
 =
 \begin{cases}
  1/n_i,&\text{if $1$ belongs to a valid copy of type $i$},\\
  0,&\text{if $1\in U_\omega$}.
 \end{cases}
 \label{eq:projection-diagonal}$$ The valid copy in the first case is unique.
